questions.question_text: Which of the following is a direct band-gap semiconductor?
questions.answer: GaAs is a direct bandgap semiconductor because the conduction band minimum and valence band maximum occur at the same k-value.

questions.question_text: In an indirect band-gap semiconductor, the conduction band minimum and valence band maximum are located....................
options: At the same energy and momentum
At different energies but same momentum
At the same energy but different momentum
At different energies and different momentum
questions.answer: Indirect bandgap means the extrema of the bands occur at different wavevectors (k), and they necessarily correspond to different energy levels.

questions.question_text: At a finite temperature, the probability of electron occupancy at the Fermi level Ef is:
questions.answer: Based on the Fermi-Dirac distribution, at E = Ef, the probability f(E) is exactly 0.5 for any T > 0.

questions.question_text: Which computational method uses the atomic orbital approach to determine electronic band structure?
questions.answer: The tight-binding method (also known as LCAO) treats electrons as being tightly bound to their atoms and calculates the band structure using a linear combination of atomic orbitals.

questions.question_text: As temperature increases, the Fermi level in an n-type semiconductor .....................
questions.answer: With increasing temperature, the semiconductor tends to become intrinsic, causing the Fermi level to shift from near the conduction band toward the center of the bandgap.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: The Shockley–Read–Hall (SRH) mechanism describes .....................
questions.answer: SRH recombination is a non-radiative process where charge carriers are captured by deep-level traps (impurities or defects) within the bandgap.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: A light-emitting diode (LED) emits light when it is .....................
questions.answer: LEDs emit light via electroluminescence when forward biased, which allows electrons and holes to recombine at the junction.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Under which bias condition does the depletion region width increase in a PN junction?
questions.answer: Reverse bias increases the potential barrier and pulls majority carriers away from the junction, widening the depletion region.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents an intra band transition?
questions.answer: Intra-band transitions occur within the same energy band (e.g., an electron moving from one energy state to another within the conduction band), which is typical for free carriers.

questions.question_text: The four-point probe method is superior to the two-point probe method because it .....................
options: Eliminates contact and lead resistance errors
questions.answer: By using separate pairs of probes for current injection and voltage measurement, the four-point probe method removes the influence of contact and lead resistance from the result.

questions.question_text: The hot-point probe method is primarily used to .....................
questions.answer: It is a quick qualitative method to distinguish between n-type and p-type semiconductors based on the thermoelectric effect.

questions.question_text: A quantum dot exhibits confinement in .....................
questions.answer: Quantum dots are 0D structures where charge carriers are confined in all three spatial dimensions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a direct band-gap semiconductor?
questions.answer: Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) is a classic direct bandgap semiconductor widely used in optoelectronics.

questions.question_text: In an indirect band-gap semiconductor, the conduction band minimum and valence band maximum are located..............
options: At the same energy and momentum
At different energies but same momentum
At the same energy but different momentum
At different energies and different momentum
questions.answer: In an indirect bandgap material, the minimum of the conduction band and maximum of the valence band occur at different values of crystal momentum (k).

questions.question_text: At a finite temperature, the probability of electron occupancy at the Fermi level Ef is:
questions.answer: The Fermi-Dirac distribution states that the probability of occupation at the Fermi energy (E = Ef) is exactly 1/2 for any temperature > 0 K.

questions.question_text: Which computational method uses the atomic orbital approach to determine electronic band structure?
questions.answer: The tight-binding method, also known as LCAO (Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals), constructs energy bands using atomic orbital functions.

questions.question_text: As temperature increases, the Fermi level in an n-type semiconductor ..................
questions.answer: As temperature increases, more intrinsic carriers are generated, causing the Fermi level to shift downward from near the conduction band towards the intrinsic level (middle of the gap).
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: The Shockley–Read–Hall (SRH) mechanism describes .................
questions.answer: The SRH recombination mechanism involves defect states or "traps" within the bandgap that facilitate the recombination of electrons and holes.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: A light-emitting diode (LED) emits light when it is ........................
questions.answer: An LED emits light under forward bias, where electrons and holes are injected across the junction and recombine to release photons.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Under which bias condition does the depletion region width increase in a PN junction?
questions.answer: Reverse bias pulls majority charge carriers away from the junction, increasing the width of the depletion region.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents an intra band transition?
questions.answer: Intra-band transitions involve a carrier moving from one energy state to another within the same band, also known as free-carrier absorption.

questions.question_text: Fermi’s Golden Rule is used to determine the ........................
questions.answer: Fermi's Golden Rule computes the transition probability rate for quantum systems subjected to perturbations.

questions.question_text: When upward transitions exceed downward transitions, what condition is achieved?
questions.answer: If upward transitions (absorption) exceed downward transitions (emission), there is net absorption, i.e. optical loss. Optical gain requires downward transitions to exceed upward ones (population inversion).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major loss mechanism in photovoltaic cells?
questions.answer: Recombination of generated electron-hole pairs before they can be collected at the electrodes represents a primary efficiency loss in solar cells.

questions.question_text: The four-point probe method is superior to the two-point probe method because it ........................
options: Eliminates contact and lead resistance errors
questions.answer: By separating current supply and voltage measurement, the four-point probe method bypasses the voltage drop across the contacts, providing accurate sheet resistance.

questions.question_text: The hot-point probe method is primarily used to ........................
questions.answer: The hot-point probe test uses the thermoelectric (Seebeck) effect to determine the majority carrier type of a semiconductor.

questions.question_text: C–V measurements in a PN junction or MOS capacitor are used to extract ........................
questions.answer: Capacitance-Voltage (C-V) profiling is fundamentally used to extract built-in potential and doping concentration profiles in junctions.

questions.question_text: The Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) describes ........................
options: Distribution of charge carriers under external forces and scattering
Diffusion of photons in a medium
questions.answer: The BTE evaluates the statistical distribution of particles experiencing external driving forces, diffusion, and scattering processes.

questions.question_text: A quantum dot exhibits confinement in ........................
questions.answer: In a quantum dot, charge carriers are quantum-confined in all three spatial dimensions, behaving as an artificial atom.

questions.question_text: Which is NOT a typical property of carbon nanotubes (CNTs)?
questions.answer: Carbon nanotubes are renowned for having extremely high thermal conductivity, making "poor thermal conductivity" an incorrect property.

questions.question_text: In Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), surface topography is obtained by ........................
options: Detecting cantilever deflection of a sharp tip scanning the surface
questions.answer: AFM works by physically scanning a sharp tip across the surface and measuring the tiny deflections of the cantilever to map out topography.

questions.question_text: TCAD (Technology Computer-Aided Design) tools are primarily used to ........................
options: Predict semiconductor device behavior before fabrication
questions.answer: TCAD simulations model device fabrication processes and electrical behavior computationally, saving time and money prior to physical manufacturing.
